[RTIM.14.16] **A failing case names the faults it met.** When a case fails,
for any reason, the interpreter **must** report with it every fault event
([NCBK.2.8]) the case's engine raised while the interpreter drove it, in
stream order. Each one names its kind, the mock-clock instant of the step that
raised it, the rule whose activation it abandoned where the event names one,
and what the event gives of its cause: a `ComputationError`'s kind
([LERR.1.4.9]), a `TypeError`'s schema and slot ([RARC.5.2.7]), a
`BoundsError`'s cap. For a case that passes, the interpreter **may** report
them.

A fault does not fail a case by itself. A case is judged by its assertions
([LTSL.8.5]) and by [RTIM.14.14], and a test may drive a rule into a fault on
purpose.

An activation a fault abandons makes none of the observations its rule would
have made, so the assertions over them fail with a count of zero. Without the
fault beside them, that count points at the rule's conditions and not at the
fault.
